stumbles.quote: Ettin's tokenizer spends 376 tokens per abstract
stumbles.why: Ettin is never explained (a model family?), and the baseline tokenizer is not described. The reader can't tell if it's a general-domain tokenizer.

stumbles.quote: Yes, a life-sciences vocabulary makes Ettin cheaper on PubMed text, provided the pre-tokenizer changes with it.
stumbles.why: The headline 'Yes' is conditional. The 8% saving with the GPT-2 pre-tokenizer that Ettin actually uses sits uneasily with it. It is also unclear whether 'cheaper' means fewer tokens or compute cost.

stumbles.quote: Oskar asked on 2026-11-06 whether "we [could] create an entirely custom domain Ettin model with custom token table ... for life sciences".
stumbles.why: Oskar is an unexplained name. The quote is elided and bracketed, and it appears with no context.

stumbles.quote: This experiment answers the token-table half of that question.
stumbles.why: The two halves of the question are never laid out, so the reader must infer what the other half is.
It names a separate experiment with no location or explanation. It is unclear whether it exists yet.

stumbles.quote: so no published clinical ModernBERT has tried a retrained table
stumbles.why: This is a broad claim about all published models. It rests only on two models that were named, and it doesn't follow from them. BioClinical ModernBERT and Clinical ModernBERT are not explained.

point: Retraining a 50K BPE vocabulary on PubMed cuts token counts by 21% if the pre-tokenizer splits on whitespace only, but by just 8% with Ettin's GPT-2 pre-tokenizer, because that pre-tokenizer breaks terms like GLP-1 apart.
